penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: A $49 lifetime deal to individual developers/indie teams requires very high volume of one-time purchasers to generate meaningful recurring revenue; no subscription means no compounding MRR, and the segment is notoriously price-sensitive and high-churn for tools.

rationale: The pain is real — small teams want a lightweight feature request tracker without SaaS subscription overhead — but the buyer is a price-sensitive individual developer or small ISV who explicitly rejects ongoing payment, making sustainable revenue generation very difficult. A $49 lifetime deal requires hundreds of sales to matter, and this segment (solo devs on Stack Exchange software-recs) has demonstrated strong resistance to any paid tools. Willingness to pay for subscriptions is low by design; willingness to pay for one-time purchases is higher but the economics don't support a solo operator building and maintaining a product at that price point. Total after penalty is 4.1, well below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: Not recommended. The micro-service would be a simple web-based feature request board with file attachment support, sold as a $49 one-time purchase or self-hosted download. BUILD is feasible with Claude + a simple form/database + Stripe one-time payment, but SELL and MAINTAIN are the problems: the target buyer actively avoids paying for software, the market is crowded with free alternatives (GitHub Issues, Trello, Linear free tier), and a lifetime-deal model means zero recurring revenue — Youval would need hundreds of sales to generate meaningful income. Support requests from self-hosters are also likely to be high-touch. A solo non-technical operator cannot profitably build and maintain this at the price point the market will accept.
notes: Total 4.1 < min_total_to_validate (5.5) after b2c_at_scale_needed penalty. Primary weaknesses: buyer_clarity=5 (individual devs, not business buyers with budgets), willingness_to_pay=5 (explicitly rejects subscription; lifetime deal economics are poor), responsiveness_signal=1 (single Stack Exchange post, no demand validation). Drop recommended.
